facility_roles.quote: CDF is one of two detectors positioned along the four-mile Tevatron accelerator ring.

facility_roles.note: The Tevatron proton-antiproton beams that CDF records are produced and accelerated entirely at Fermilab.

intervals.label: proposed (FNAL-E-0741)
intervals.note: INSPIRE gives day precision (1981-08-01) but the day is very likely a database default; recorded here at month precision.

intervals.label: approved
intervals.note: Same day-precision caveat as the proposed date.

intervals.label: construction and installation (inferred bound)
intervals.locator: INSPIRE experiment record 1109361 (approval); fnal.gov Tevatron Experiments: CDF page (first collisions)
intervals.note: No source explicitly labels this period "construction"; it is the sourced gap between CDF's 1982 approval and the first recorded Tevatron collisions. Status is an inference, not a sourced label; the two dates bounding it are each independently sourced.

intervals.label: first Tevatron proton-antiproton collisions observed by CDF
intervals.quote: Physicists observed the first proton-antiproton collisions produced by the Tevatron on Oct. 13, 1985.

intervals.label: engineering run and first physics results
intervals.note: Year precision only; source gives no month.
intervals.quote: The first physics results were obtained during 1987, in an engineering run, and in 1988/89, in a year-long run.

intervals.label: Run I data-taking, ending Spring 1996
intervals.note: Start left null: sources describe continuous 1987-1996 running with detector upgrades (silicon vertex detector installed 1992) rather than a single clean 'Run I start' distinct from the 1987/1988-89 runs above.
intervals.quote: The Collider run ended in Spring 96 with a total luminosity of 110 pb**(-1) recorded on tape.

intervals.label: shutdown for Main Injector-era upgrade
intervals.note: Quote reproduces a typo ("ans") present in the source text verbatim.
intervals.quote: The detector will be upgraded ... for the next Collider run with the Main Injector ... Upgrade is complete ans data taking has resumed (March 2001).

intervals.label: Run II
intervals.locator: INSPIRE experiment record 1109361, description field; Tevatron shutdown Sept. 30, 2011 per Fermilab Newsroom
intervals.quote: Upgrade is complete ans data taking has resumed (March 2001).

intervals.label: Tevatron shutdown; CDF data-taking ends
intervals.locator: news.fnal.gov, "Tevatron shuts down, but analysis continues" (2011-09); cdf.fnal.gov home page
intervals.note: cdf.fnal.gov confirms: "studies high energy proton-antiproton collisions from data collected through 2011." Status recorded as completed (data-taking over; the collaboration continues to analyze the archived dataset, e.g. its 2022 W-mass measurement).
intervals.quote: When the Tevatron shut down on Sept. 30, 2011, scientists first stopped the CDF and DZero detectors. ... It took about a month to fully shut down the CDF detector, including time to remove its cooling fluids and gases.

quantity.note: The original 1988 NIM detector-overview paper (src:colliders-historical-cdf-nim-1988-detector-overview) instead gives "5000 t" for the as-built detector; the two figures are not reconciled here (different era/configuration or rounding). fnal.gov figure preferred per source hierarchy (official facility site ranks above a detector paper).
quantity.quote: The 4,500-ton detector sits more than four stories tall and is composed of more than 1 million individual detector elements.

quantity.note: The 1988 NIM detector-overview paper (src:colliders-historical-cdf-nim-1988-detector-overview) instead gives a 1.5 T field from a coil "3 m in diameter and 5 m in length" -- close to but not identical with the INSPIRE record's 1.4 T / 4.8 m length figure used here. Not reconciled; INSPIRE experiment record (rank 3) preferred over the detector paper (rank 5) per the source hierarchy.
quantity.quote: A superconducting solenoid of length 4.8 m and radius 1.5 m generates a 1.4 T magnetic field and contains tracking chambers used to detect charged particles and measure their momenta.

name: CDF
notes: INSPIRE experiment record 1109361 gives date_proposed=1981-08-01, date_approved=1982-04-01, date_started=1987-01-01, date_completed=1992-01-01. The day component on three of these four fields is 01 and two also have month 01, consistent with INSPIRE defaulting an unknown day/month to the 1st -- these are recorded here at year or year-month precision rather than day precision except date_proposed and date_approved, which are used at month precision as a conservative reading. date_started/date_completed are NOT used as the run boundaries: INSPIRE's own free-text description clarifies date_started=1987 means the first ("engineering run") physics results, and date_completed=1992 coincides with silicon vertex detector installation, not experiment end -- CDF continued operating to 2011 per cdf.fnal.gov and the 2011 Fermilab shutdown sources.

external.inspire_experiment is recorded as the bare INSPIRE recid (1109361) per the ontology §3.5 shape; the record-level `sources` list includes src:colliders-historical-cdf-inspire-experiment-record, whose url (https://inspirehep.net/experiments/1109361) contains that recid, per A20.

physics_goals.quote: Look for the production of New Physics; Measure and study the production and decay of heavy particles such as the Top and Bottom Quarks, and the W and Z bosons.
physics_goals.value: Study proton-antiproton collisions to look for new physics, and measure and study the production and decay of heavy particles such as the top and bottom quarks and the W and Z bosons

summary.plain: A giant particle detector at Fermilab, near Chicago, that watched protons and their antimatter twins smash together at nearly the speed of light. It helped find the top quark, the heaviest known building block of matter, and ran until the Tevatron collider it depended on shut down in 2011.
summary.technical: General-purpose proton-antiproton collider detector at the B0 interaction hall on the Fermilab Tevatron ring. Solenoidal tracking plus electromagnetic/hadronic calorimetry and muon systems; co-discovered the top quark with D0 in 1995. Operated from first Tevatron collisions (1985) through Run I (to spring 1996) and Run II (2001-2011), ending with the Tevatron shutdown of 30 September 2011.
